transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thanks. Well, I guess what really pushed me to come in today is... I've been having this issue at work. I work at a reception desk, and lately, every time a loud door slams, or even if someone just rolls a suitcase fast across the lobby, I jump. 

It's like my body thinks it's happening all over again. And then it takes me a good minute or so just to get my heart rate back down to normal. It's just getting really hard to get through my shifts like that.
Do these reactions seem to be connected to any particular memory or experience from your past?

Yeah, it is. It's connected to an incident that happened at work recently. Sometimes, just out of nowhere, I’ll get this picture in my head of that guest leaning over the counter and knocking the equipment toward me. It just pops up, even when I’m just trying to answer a normal call. So, yeah, those loud noises just kind of bring that specific memory right back.
Have you been avoiding certain situations or places at work since the incident happened?

Yeah, actually. I've been... well, I've been taking the back hallway whenever I can. Walking past the exact spot in the lobby where it happened... it just makes my chest tighten up. I just want to get away from it, so I try to avoid that area as much as possible.
Do you ever experience memories of the incident as if you're reliving it, like a flashback?

No, not really like a flashback. It's more like... I just get those pictures in my head that I mentioned, like a snapshot of him knocking the stuff over. But I don't feel like I'm actually back in that exact moment, reliving the whole thing. It's just the memory popping up and startle reactions to the noises.
How long have you been experiencing these startle reactions and intrusive memories since the incident happened?
Well, it's been going on for about two weeks now. Basically, ever since that guest threatened me at the front desk. That's when it all started.
Are there any specific things, like people, conversations, or activities, that you've been avoiding because they remind you of what happened?

Not really, no. I mean, other than avoiding that spot in the lobby like I mentioned, I haven't really been staying away from anything else. I still talk to my coworkers and do my normal day-to-day stuff. So, no, I haven't been avoiding any specific people or conversations... it's really just that one physical area that I try to steer clear of.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your relationships with family, friends, or coworkers since the incident happened?

Well, I haven't had major blowups or anything, but... I guess I've been a little on edge with my coworkers. I'm usually pretty careful and polite with them, but lately I hear myself snapping short answers over little things. Like, if someone asks me to repeat a confirmation number or something minor, I just kind of bite their head off. I don't mean to, it just comes out that way. But with family and friends, things have been pretty much normal.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your daily life or work since you started experiencing these reactions and memories?

Well, I'm still showing up for work, but it's definitely affecting me. My manager actually had to shorten a couple of my shifts recently. I'm just... I'm a lot slower at the reservation desk right now. And like I said about avoiding that spot in the lobby, I keep finding excuses not to cross over there when guests need help. So yeah, it's definitely causing some issues with how I do my job.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers, even when you're not at work?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or anything like that when I'm at home or out running errands. It's really just when I'm at work, near that lobby area, that I feel tense. But outside of work, I feel pretty normal in terms of looking out for danger.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, when I'm off the clock, I still like doing the same things I usually do. I still watch my regular shows, catch up with friends... things like that. It's really just work that's been tough, but my hobbies and normal weekend stuff are pretty much the same.
Do you have trouble falling or staying asleep since the incident happened?

No, my sleep has been fine, actually. I haven't really had any trouble falling asleep, and I usually sleep through the night just fine. Once I'm home and away from work, I can just wind down and sleep like normal.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're to blame for what happened or that you should have done something to prevent it?

No, I haven't really been thinking like that. I mean, I'm just a receptionist, you know? I was just sitting at my desk when it all happened. There wasn't really anything I could have done to stop it, so I don't feel like it's my fault or anything. It was just a really bad situation that happened while I was on shift.
Have you felt less interested in things you normally enjoy doing since the incident at work?

I think you asked me that a little bit ago, but no, not really. I'm still doing the same stuff I usually do when I'm not at work. I still like watching my shows and hanging out with friends. It's just work that's been hard to deal with.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of guilt or shame related to the incident at work?

No, not really. I think that kind of goes back to what I was just saying about not feeling like it was my fault. I don't have any guilt or shame about it, no. I was just sitting at the front desk doing my job when it all went down, so there's nothing for me to feel guilty about.
Have you avoided talking about the incident with others?

No, I haven't really been avoiding talking about it. I mean, my friends and family all wanted to know what happened, so I've told them the story. It's not something I'm trying to hide from or anything, it's just... it's just a lot to process, you know? But talking about it hasn't been an issue for me.
Do you feel like you're always on the lookout for something bad to happen, even when there's no obvious reason to think that?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm definitely a bit jumpy at work now, just because of what happened, but outside of that? Not really. I'm not, like, constantly looking over my shoulder when I'm at the grocery store or anything like that. It's really just when I'm sitting at that front desk.
